transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I've called us together because the state regulator has requested our internal-investigation materials related to the alleged improper procurement practices, and we have ten business days from the date of the request to respond. The current draft response proposes continuing with the existing investigation, providing a general status update, and preserving all potentially privileged material. Before I approve this response for submission, I'm conducting our routine pre-submission review. I'd like compliance counsel and conflicts counsel to report any issues that could affect this filing. Please walk me through anything you've identified.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to flag a significant issue. This week I confirmed with the regulator's staff that their cooperation protocol grants voluntary-disclosure cooperation credit only if the company makes a voluntary disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting, produces factual interview summaries prepared by the independent investigator as part of the conflict-driven reinvestigation, and withholds only legal advice and attorney work product. The required factual interview summaries must be submitted with the voluntary disclosure itself — the reinvestigation is the mechanism for producing them, not a basis to defer or omit them. The staff emphasized that this fifth-business-day deadline and the factual-summary requirement remain operative even if investigative remediation is needed. Without producing those independent-investigator summaries, we cannot claim voluntary-disclosure cooperation credit. I had not circulated this confirmation earlier because it arrived after the response draft was prepared.

transcript.text: Elena, I need to raise a critical conflicts issue. My conflict review, completed this morning, found that the company's existing investigator previously represented a procurement witness in an unrelated matter involving the same allegations. Because of this conflict, the investigator must be removed and the factual investigation must be re-performed by an independent investigator. I have not yet updated the matter's conflict log because the review was just completed this morning. This directly affects our draft response — we cannot represent to the regulator that we are 'continuing with the existing investigation' when that investigation is conflict-tainted and must be redone. This also aligns with what Samir just raised: the regulator requires factual interview summaries prepared by an independent investigator, and our current investigator does not satisfy that requirement.

transcript.text: Elena, Maya's conflicts finding and my protocol confirmation together show that our draft response needs substantial revision. To summarize the two operational problems: First, we cannot claim voluntary-disclosure cooperation credit unless we submit factual interview summaries prepared by an independent investigator with our disclosure by the fifth business day after the review meeting. Second, the current investigator is conflicted and must be replaced, meaning the factual investigation must be re-performed. The practical implication is that we need to move quickly to engage an independent investigator who can conduct the necessary interviews and prepare the factual summaries within the cooperation-credit deadline. The draft's proposal to simply 'continue with the existing investigation' and give a general status update would not satisfy the protocol's requirements and would forfeit cooperation credit. I'd recommend we revise the response to commit to independent reinvestigation and production of the required factual summaries on the protocol's timeline. I should also note that I have not yet circulated my staff confirmation in writing, so we should make sure the full details are documented before submission.
